hypotheses.title: Beta Decoupling with Idiosyncratic Risk Normalization
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Evaluates decoupling between intraday pricing dynamics (close / vwap) and 60-day market sensitivity (beta_last_60_days_spy) alongside idiosyncratic variance shocks (unsystematic_risk_last_30_days / unsystematic_risk_last_360_days). Equities undergoing temporary idiosyncratic variance spikes while their correlation to systematic market beta decouples represent temporary non-fundamental liquidity dislocations that mean-revert strongly.
confounders: Genuine corporate solvency events that permanently elevate idiosyncratic risk without mean-reversion
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if elevated idiosyncratic variance persists and indicates structural bankruptcy rather than temporary liquidity dislocation.

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Customer Return Shock Spillover with Liquidity Exhaustion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Customer return shocks propagate to suppliers over a multi-day horizon due to gradual information diffusion. Propagating the signal through exponential decay (ts_decay_exp_window(..., 10, 0.5)) and weighting by low trading volume (1 - group_rank(volume / adv20, subindustry)) exploits quiet institutional under-reaction before the customer shock is fully reflected in supplier equity prices.
confounders: Sudden supplier contract cancellation rendering historical customer return signals irrelevant
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if customer return signals have already been fully priced in by market makers on Day 0.

hypotheses.title: Options Put/Call Open Interest Sentiment Interacted with Cycle Extrema Timing
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Options Put/Call Open Interest (pcr_oi_30) is an inverted institutional hedging sentiment indicator; excessive put OI indicates bearish retail crowding. Interacting contrarian put/call sentiment with the temporal difference between the 30-day peak and trough (ts_argmax(high, 30) - ts_argmin(low, 30)) isolates equities at the end of exhaustive downtrends where bearish put demand is peaked and forward recovery is asymmetric.
confounders: Sustained institutional hedging driven by material non-public fundamental deterioration
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if high put open interest accurately forecasts persistent downside continuation.
